newsitem.title: USA: Ill.Gov repeals state takeover of commuter airport.
newsitem.headline: Ill.Gov repeals state takeover of commuter airport.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar has signed a bill repealing the state takeover of a Chicago lakefront commuter airport.
Edgar signed the bill Tuesday as part of a state and city agreement to resolve a dispute over Meigs Field, which Chicago Mayor Richard Daley plans to convert to a lakefront park.

The city had closed the commuter airport, used mainly by business and state aircraft, last year as part of its plan to create a $27 million bond-financed nature park. State officials responded with a takeover that landed the dispute in state court.

In a settlement announced in January, city officials agreed to reopen the airport, make improvements and keep it open for five more years. State officials agreed to repeal the legislation that allowed them to seize it before Chicago could begin demolition.

Illinois Senate President James "Pate" Philip, R-Wood Dale, said during the legislative session last month that the state should reconsider its end of the bargain, contending that Chicago officials had not followed through with promised improvements.
The repeal law creates a 13-member advisory panel with city, state and legislative representation to ensure improvements are completed.
